headline: Computational models resolve context-specific RNA regulation and technical artifacts
label: Computational Rna Regulation Methods
summary: New calibrated datasets and benchmarks test splicing, eQTL, and chromatin-linked regulation models against experimental and DNA-based ground truth.
synthesis: The dominant thread is context-resolved inference of RNA regulation coupled with explicit correction of measurement artifacts and validation against orthogonal ground truth. FastGxC and HELIX model context dependence in eQTL mapping and splicing prediction, while UniversalEPI and MPRabc extend model-based inference to enhancer-promoter interactions. Artifact control is the sharper novelty: StringTie3 separates nascent from mature transcripts and filters poly(A)-priming artifacts, PATTY corrects Tn5 open-chromatin bias in CUT&Tag, and a Bayesian framework estimates mosaic Y loss from bulk RNA-seq validated against DNA-based LOY. OpenSplice provides a calibrated dataset of over 590,000 variants across more than 600 exons for benchmarking, and COTAN models zero counts directly rather than log-normalizing. Not all items share this emphasis; the lncRNA-T2D, MHC haplotype, and somatic CNA studies apply related statistical decomposition to population and aging questions.
